Planning to build a Linux PC for my gf

Anymore, not really. Driver support has gotten much, much better in recent years. Only thing I'd recommend is avoiding an nVidia graphics chipset. It's not that they don't work, but driver support is more of a pain. There are no open source drivers for nVidia that support 3D acceleration. They'll work out of the box- the open source driver used has limited functionality but will work. But that's a known issue and there's a lot of info online. Or, you can just avoid using nVidia.

There are proprietary drivers for Nvidia though, and they work well. If proprietary drivers are not an issue for OP, than this really isn't a problem at all. Historically the proprietary NVIDIA drivers have been better than the opensource drivers for NVIDIA and AMD.

Any modern hardware should run fine on Linux. If you're worried, choose a machine, then do a quick search for it and the distro you choose. If you don't see any problems, then you should be good to go.

I've heard bad things about Optimus(nVidia), so maybe steer clear of that and stick with AMD or Intel. She doesn't sound like she needs it(it may also only be in laptops, I'm not sure).

http://www.thelinuxrain.com/articles/the-state-of-nvidia-optimus-on-linux

The Optimus problems are largely in the past for the integrated Intel/Nvidia combo cards. The newest propriatary Nvidia drivers now have a little radio button that lets you swap back and forth between the embedded cards. It's hella easier than it was just a year or two ago.
